source_name: Vreme — Kosovo economy coverage
source_subtype: weekly magazine (has sr and en editions)
why_relevant: Independent Serbian weekly producing structural pieces on dinar circulation and the wave of Serbian-institution closures in Kosovo, with counts of branches and financial institutions in northern municipalities — quantitative organization-change signal.

source_name: Radio Slobodna Evropa / RFE-RL Balkan Service (Kosovo desk)
why_relevant: Bilingual sr/en desk with sustained, sourced reporting on the CBK euro-only regulation and its effect on Serbia-paid employees; explanatory pieces are good for glossary building and actor identification across both Pristina and Belgrade sides.

source_name: N1 (sr) — Kosovo/CBK coverage
why_relevant: Regional commercial broadcaster carrying CBK statements in Serbian, including operational detail on which banks operate in the north — useful cross-check against Belgrade-aligned and Pristina-aligned framings.

source_name: Glas Amerike (VOA Serbian service)
why_relevant: Serbian-language service with detailed operational reporting on the police closure of Poštanska štedionica branches, including staff detentions — direct organization/staffing events reported in sr.

source_name: Quipu GmbH — News / Newsroom (ProCredit Holding IT subsidiary, regional office & card personalisation centre in Prishtina)
why_relevant: Quipu is the captive IT/processing vendor of ProCredit Bank Kosovo and runs its card processing & personalisation centre in Kosovo serving 25+ financial institutions. Its news posts announce Kosovo-specific go-lives (mobile banking app, digital onboarding with FintechOS, next-gen 3DS e-commerce gateway) that reveal ProCredit Kosovo org/tech changes months before the bank says anything, and its Prishtina office is a continuous hiring signal.

source_name: Quipu job postings on KosovaJob (Prishtina office)
source_subtype: employer page on national job board
why_relevant: Direct evidence of vendor hiring in Kosovo for bank-implementation roles (Implementation Engineer, Job-ID 20016, Prishtina). Role titles and team names in these ads expose which banking modules Quipu is rolling out locally and how the Kosovo delivery team is growing.

source_name: MELLON Kosova (Mellon Albania Sh.p.k. – Kosovo Branch) job ads on KosovaJob
why_relevant: Mellon Kosova (est. 2013, Prishtina) services EFT/POS terminals, ATMs, queuing and cash-management machines for Kosovo retail banks. Its Hardware Services Engineer / Field & Lab Service Engineer ads are the clearest recurring signal of ATM/POS estate work and headcount growth at Kosovo banks.

source_name: Mellon Group of Companies — corporate site (companies / countries pages)
why_relevant: Parent of Mellon Kosova; publishes country structure, subsidiary leadership and service lines (transaction automation, back-office outsourcing for banks). Country-manager and new-office announcements here are the indirect route to Kosovo bank vendor relationships.

source_name: Best Vision Balkan (Prishtina) — LinkedIn company page & KosovaJob ads
why_relevant: Kosovo-based development arm of a core-banking software house; its ads describe work on 'software products aimed at improving the operation of small and medium-sized banks and financial institutions'. Headcount growth here maps to core-banking projects reaching Kosovo/regional banks.

source_name: Payten (ASEE / Asseco South Eastern Europe) — corporate site & country pages
why_relevant: ASEE/Payten is a leading regional supplier of ATM/POS maintenance, outsourcing and card processing; ASEE's own reporting states Payten is building market share in Albania and Kosovo. Country pages, customer references and management/country-manager listings are the indirect route to Kosovo bank estate outsourcing deals.

source_name: Asseco South Eastern Europe — annual & management reports (segment/geography commentary)
why_relevant: ASEE's consolidated management reports contain explicit geographic commentary (e.g. payments market-share build in Albania and Kosovo) and segment revenue drivers such as POS/ATM maintenance. A listed issuer's report is a high-credibility, dated statement about Kosovo vendor activity that no Kosovo bank would publish itself.

source_name: Halcom — solutions / references pages (e-banking, qualified digital certificates, SR & SL localisations)
why_relevant: Halcom's Hal E-Bank is reported as used across nine markets including Kosovo, with Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo cited as a first mobile-bank user. Vendor reference/customer pages are the indirect confirmation of which Kosovo bank runs which e-banking stack, and Halcom's regional office/leadership pages carry country-manager signals.

source_name: Printec Group — corporate site, partners page and news (Printec L.L.C. Prishtina)
why_relevant: Printec operates a Kosovo legal entity (PRINTEC L.L.C., Prishtinë) and supplies e-payment systems, branch automation, banking software and card applications to CEE banks, partnering with NCR, Verifone, De La Rue and Worldline. Its news/partners pages and event write-ups are a direct pointer to Kosovo bank projects and to its own local hiring/country leadership.

source_name: Dun & Bradstreet business directory — vendor legal entities registered in Kosovo (e.g. PRINTEC L.L.C., Prishtinë)
why_relevant: Confirms which international banking-technology vendors have actually incorporated a Kosovo entity (vs. serving remotely) and often names local executives and employee counts — the cheapest way to build the vendor actor map before searching for their announcements.

source_name: IPKO Telecommunications — business/enterprise news (critical infrastructure for banks)
why_relevant: IPKO was announced as PriBank's strategic partner for the critical infrastructure and security services underpinning its banking platforms — an end-to-end designed and implemented solution. Telco/DC integrators announcing bank wins is exactly the indirect route around Kosovo's private-bank procurement opacity.

source_name: Kosovo Banking Association (Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës) — events, committees and The Kosovo Banker
why_relevant: Its 'Cyber Security in the Banking Sector' forums and committee-chairmanship elections name the bank executives who chair them (a direct leadership-move signal) and list the vendors who sponsor/speak — effectively a curated, recurring roster of which security and payments suppliers are courting Kosovo banks.

source_name: STIKK — Kosovo ICT Association member directory and member profiles
why_relevant: STIKK covers 100+ members and ~60% of Kosovo's ICT labour market; member profiles state each firm's specialisation and association memberships (e.g. Panamic ICT is described as a member of payments and banking associations in Kosovo). This is the single best enumerable list of local integrators that could be partnering with banks/PSPs — the actor map for the whole cell.

source_name: CACTTUS (Prishtina) — company site, STIKK profile and vendor-partner listings
why_relevant: Described as Kosovo's leading ICT services company (system integration, cybersecurity, business solutions, ICT audit) and appears in international vendor partner directories (e.g. Kemp). Local integrators publish their vendor accreditations and hire against won projects — an indirect read on which security/infra stack Kosovo banks are buying.

source_name: Vendor partner-locator directories (Worldline business partners, Kemp partner finder, and equivalents at NCR Atleos / Verifone / Diebold Nixdorf)
why_relevant: Global vendors publish searchable partner directories with country filters. Filtering these on Kosovo/XK enumerates the authorised local resellers and integrators for payments, ATM and security hardware — the practical substitute for a non-existent public procurement trail.

source_name: Compass Plus Technologies — customer success stories (Quipu processing case study)
why_relevant: A card-processing vendor's published case study on Quipu documents the processing platform behind ProCredit's Kosovo card operations. Case-study pages are exactly the 'supplier announces the win' artefact the cell targets, and they date the underlying platform decision.

source_name: KOBIL — ProCredit Bank / Quipu success story (security vendor case study)
why_relevant: Security-vendor case study naming ProCredit/Quipu and the modernisation of online-banking authentication. Cybersecurity vendors are among the most willing to publish named bank references, making them a reliable indirect channel into Kosovo bank technology and org change.

source_name: FintechOS — Kosovo digital-onboarding partnership references
why_relevant: Quipu's own newsroom states the ProCredit Bank Kosovo digital-onboarding solution was built in partnership with FintechOS; the fintech vendor side of such a partnership typically publishes its own release and customer page, giving a second, independently dated confirmation of a Kosovo bank project.

source_name: Enterprise Europe Network — partnering-opportunity notices from Kosovo cybersecurity/IT firms
why_relevant: EEN profiles are self-filed by Kosovo suppliers seeking outsourcing/supplier agreements and describe their capabilities, target sectors and partnering intent. It surfaces small local security vendors that never appear in press coverage but do sell penetration testing and compliance work into banks.

source_name: KosovaJob — cross-employer keyword watch for banking-technology vendor roles
why_relevant: The dominant Kosovo job board and the single highest-yield hiring source for this cell: it carried both the Quipu Implementation Engineer and the MELLON Kosova Hardware Services Engineer ads. Ads expire, so it must be harvested continuously rather than searched retrospectively.

source_name: Kosovo Banking Association (Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës) — News & events feed
why_relevant: The KBA is the convening body for Kosovo's banking sector. Its news feed publishes roundtable, conference and award write-ups that name individuals with exact current title and employer (e.g. CEO Petrit Balija; IFC country officer; visiting association presidents). Dated, self-published, precise — an authoritative weak signal for leadership moves and for which institutions are staffing up.

source_name: KBA Banking Training Centre — training catalogue (Trainings)
why_relevant: Course catalogue of the accredited KBA training centre (first in region to offer the European Foundation Certificate in Banking, EFCB). Course topics and scheduling reveal where banks are building capability (blockchain, financial crime/fraud & cyber, sanctions, capital markets, private banking) — a leading indicator of new roles and reorganised units. Trainer bios also name serving bank managers.

source_name: Kosova Finance Forum / Kosova Business Forum — speakers roster
why_relevant: The single richest speaker-bio source in the cell: KFF advertises 50+ regional and international financial-sector speakers per edition, each listed with photo, exact job title and institution, on a dated page. Ideal for detecting new CxO/deputy-governor/head-of-digital appointments and for building the actor map of Kosovo banking leadership.
